chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Sa'id, from Yunus, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said:

I asked him about what has come in the hadith that you should pray al-Zuhr when the sun (i.e. its shadow) was one stature and two statures, and one cubit and two cubits, and one foot and two feet — from this and from that. So when is this, and how is this, and the shadow can sometimes be half a foot?

He said: The hadith says 'the shadow of the stature' and does not say 'the stature of the shadow', and that is because the shadow of the stature varies — sometimes it increases and sometimes it decreases — while the upright object is always one stature, it does not change. Then he said: One cubit and two cubits, and one foot and two feet. So one cubit and two cubits became the explanation of one stature and two statures during the time in which the shadow of the stature is one cubit and the shadow of two statures is two cubits.

Thus the shadow of the stature and two statures, and one cubit and two cubits, coincide in every season, both recognized, one being interpreted by the other and supported by it. So when it was a time in which the shadow of the stature was one cubit, the prayer time would be one cubit from the shadow of the stature, and the stature would be one cubit from the shadow. So when the shadow of the stature is less or more, the prayer time would be determined by the cubit and the two cubits. So this is the interpretation of the stature and two statures, and the cubit and two cubits.

key_terms.الذراع: Al-dhira' — a cubit, a traditional unit of length (approximately 45-55 cm, from elbow to fingertip)
key_terms.الظهر: Al-Zuhr — the noon prayer, one of the five obligatory daily prayers
key_terms.القامة: Al-Qama — the upright gnomon or shadow-measuring stick; also means 'stature' (height of a standing person), used as a unit to measure shadow length
key_terms.القدم: Al-qadam — a foot, a traditional unit of length used in juristic measurement of prayer times
key_terms.ظل القامة: Shadow of the stature — the length of shadow cast by an upright gnomon, which varies by season and latitude

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq explain the different shadow measurements for the Dhuhr prayer time?
ai.summary: This hadith records a detailed jurisprudential clarification by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) on the precise timing of the Dhuhr prayer based on shadow measurements. A questioner raised an apparent contradiction in earlier hadiths that variously described the prayer time using different units — statures, cubits, and feet — and asked how these could be reconciled when shadows vary by season. The Imam resolved this by explaining that 'the shadow of the stature' (ظل القامة) is the key term: the shadow itself changes with the seasons, but the upright gnomon (qama) remains constant; and the cubit and foot measurements serve as regional or seasonal equivalents for interpreting the stature measurement, such that all the described units refer to the same moment but measured differently according to local conditions.
word_analysis: one upright (shadow length of one stature)
two statures (shadow length of two statures)

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Saeed, from Yunus, from one of his men, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about what has come in the Hadeeth that Al-Zohr would be prayed when the sun was one upright (in length of shadow) and two, and one cubit and two, and one step and two, from this and from there. So when is this? And how is this, and the shadow happens to be, at certain times, half a step?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, the shadow is referred to as one shadow upright and is not said as ‘uprightness of the shadow’, and that is (because) one shadow upright differs sometimes as more, and sometimes as less, and the upright (object) would be of one uprightness (size) for ever, not being different’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘One cubit and two cubits, and one foot and two feet. So the one cubit and two cubits came to be an explanation of the one foot and two feet during the time in which the upright shadow happens to be of one cubit, and the shadow of the two uprights statures being of two cubits.

Thus, the shadow of the upright stature and two upright statures, and one cubit and two cubits happen to be co-incidental during every time, both recognised, one of them being interpreted by the other, being supported by it. So when it was the time wherein the shadow of the stature happens to be of one cubit, it would be the time of one cubit from the shadow of the upright stature, and the upright cubit would be from the shadow. So when the upright shadow is less or more, it would be the time limited by the cubit and the two cubits. 
So this is the interpretation of the upright stature and the two upright statures, and the one cubit and the two cubits’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Salih ibn Sa‘id from Yunus from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abdullah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the meaning of Hadith that says, ’Perform al- Dhuhr Salah (prayer) when the sun is equal to one length or two, one yard or two or one step or two steps from this and from there. When is it and how is it? At certain times is half of one step.’

He (the Imam) said that in the Hadith is it said, ‘ An object’s shadow’ and not the shadow of an object’ is because the shadow of an object may appear in different sizes, sometimes longer and sometimes shorter, but an object is an object all the time and it does not change. Hadith has said that it is one yard or two yards, one step or two steps.”

Thus one yard or two yards have become explanation of one length or two lengths during the time when an object’s shadow is of the size of one yard and two object’s shadows of the size of two yards. Therefore one object’s or two objects’ shadows and one yard or two yards are in agreement with each other in times as understood one, explaining the other and supported thereby. At a given time, for example at one O’clock, when an object’s shadow is of the size of one yard the time (for Salah (prayer)) is one yard of an object’s shadow and the object is a yard of the shadow. When an object’s shadow is less or more, the time is measured in yards or two yards.
This is the explanation of one length and a yard or two yards.’” (The theme of Hadith is obvious; it only may need a little thinking to grasp it fully.)
